prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image 1 is our own low-poly grove, the edit target. Preserve its EXACT composition and geometry: same coastline, water line, horizon, hill facets, ruins, roads, all individual palm positions, tree sizes, lean directions, blade shapes, cast shadows and cloud outlines.
Correct only palette and uniform flat shading. The palm crowns are presently too bright and candy green. Make them deeper, muted olive/forest green with a small amount of fresh sunlit green at the upper blades, close to these intended sRGB swatches: dark under-blades #283C28, mature mid-blades #4C6134, sunward blades #83964B, youngest tips #A0AD52. Only 2–3 such SOLID fills per tiny crown, most crown area dark/mid. Occasional old blades straw #A78A4D, never uniformly neon grass green. Leave sky, sea and ground overall warm/cool relationships in place.
Make every visible polygon a perfectly uniform solid flat color. REMOVE all residual soft gradients, noise, grain and smooth shading: the large sea region should be a few clean flat turquoise planes with no ripple or grain; sky and cloud polygon faces uniform too. Trunks flat pale grey or grey brown, no bark texture. Terrain facets remain broad solid ochre and muted sage, buildings flat warm grey and dark blue-grey holes. Crisp angular edges, shadows are flat polygons. A handsome actual low-poly game visualization with no textures anywhere. No text or watermark. Same framing and largest native landscape PNG.
